01 / On the desk

A build with a little character.

Part tool, part personal project. A custom keyboard is a collection of small decisions you get to make your own.

Cream on the outside.
Oblivion underneath my fingers.

The Think6.5 V2 is the centerpiece here: a cream case, GMK Oblivion keycaps, and Gateron Black Ink switches. These are the parts in my build.

02 / The person behind the desk

Hi, I'm Ivan.

Mechanical Engineering
Vanderbilt University
From Vancouver, BC

I like projects where design choices have consequences. How does a shape change performance? How does a material change sound? What happens when we approach a problem with better data?

I'm studying Mechanical Engineering at Vanderbilt with a minor in Data Science, and exploring optimization and aerospace. Building custom keyboards is one of my favorite hobbies, and a small reminder that engineering can be personal, too.

04 / An introduction to the hobby

What's the keyboard obsession?

A keyboard is something I use every day. Building one lets me choose how it looks, how it feels, and how it sounds.

01 / The feel of a keypress

It starts with a switch.

Under each keycap is a switch. Linear switches move without a deliberate tactile bump, tactile switches add a noticeable bump, and clicky switches add a click. The Black Inks in my build are linear.

Same keyboard, different switches: a different feel under your fingers.
